rubrics.criterion: Each starter-template convention that the validation sweep (script/validate-data/index.ts) and the GHES sync (script/sync-ghes/index.ts) currently share — resolving a workflow's properties/*.properties.json companion file, interpreting the iconName field (embedded `octicon <name>` references vs plain svg-file names), the blank.yml exemption, the deployments-folder creator requirement, the code-scanning-folder eligibility rule, and partner-creator classification — is moved so that a maintainer changing that convention edits exactly one shared definition (or one parameterized definition) that both scripts' behavior derives from, instead of the fragments currently contributed from script/validate-data/templatePaths.ts, script/validate-data/templateIcons.ts, and the two entry scripts.
rubrics.rationale: This is the case's central shotgun-surgery responsibility: the injected diff deliberately spreads one conceptually unified convention layer across helper modules, both entry scripts, and two settings files, and the graded fact is precisely that the scatter itself is gone.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair no convention implementation is reachable only through runtime string resolution: every place a script acts on a starter-template convention names the code that implements it statically (a direct import, call, or module reference), so a reader of either entry script can see which implementation runs without consulting a key in script/validate-data/settings.json or script/sync-ghes/settings.json.
rubrics.rationale: The settings-driven slot maps are the mechanism that makes the injected scatter hard to follow (slot string in one file, registered rule name in another, implementation in a third); the reportable outcome is that this indirection no longer routes shared conventions, while a simple non-convention use of settings (folders, partners, categories) remains acceptable.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidated conventions are located in a place both scripts use directly and symmetrically: the validation sweep and the GHES sync both obtain the properties-path, icon-reference, blank-template, deployment-folder, code-scanning-folder, and partner-creator rules from the same shared module or set of definitions (no convention owned by one consumer with the other still calling a stale private copy, and no convention whose GHES-side availability depends on a side-effect import of another script's helpers).
rubrics.rationale: The injected state makes the GHES script depend on importing the validation script's helper modules merely so that its slot lookups resolve, which is why the repair must be graded on cross-script wiring, not just on how many fragments one script consolidates.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave the consolidation one-sided: either entry script still carrying its own locally-defined convention helper (for example a local `isBlankTemplate`/`isDeploymentFolder` pair in script/validate-data/index.ts or a local `isPartnerCreator`/`isCodeScanningFolder` pair in script/sync-ghes/index.ts) while other conventions were consolidated, or still calling an implementation registered elsewhere through a slot name, fails this item.
rubrics.rationale: The most likely incomplete repair for this instance is consolidating the easily visible fragments (paths and icons) while leaving the four fragment functions defined inside the entry scripts untouched, because those look like ordinary local helpers rather than part of the shared convention layer.

rubrics.criterion: The validation sweep's embedded-icon detection keeps its existing semantics: a workflow whose iconName does not start with `octicon ` (a plain svg name) is still validated by probing an svg file under the repository icons folder for that name, while a value of the form `octicon <name>` is still accepted without by-name file probing and is still rejected only when it carries no icon name after the prefix.
rubrics.rationale: Both the validation flavor (prefix `octicon ` followed by at least something, checked with a regex on the reference) and the GHES flavor (`startsWith("octicon")`) were injected as separate registered fragments; unifying them around the GHES prefix flavor is exactly the silent-risk subclass specific to this case, because the current 174-template corpus contains only plain slugs and well-formed `octicon <name>` values that both classify identically.

rubrics.criterion: For the GHES sync, whichever shared icon convention it now uses, a workflow with an embedded `octicon`-style reference still results in no svg asset being copied into the sync's file list, and a workflow with a plain svg-name iconName still results in that svg asset's path being added to the list of files pulled over for the ghes branch.
rubrics.rationale: The GHES icon-kind decision is expressed through a consumer-side selection between two flavors whose disagreement over unusual values (for example the value 'octicon' with no trailing name, or 'octicons/foo') is indistinguishable on the current corpus, so the copy decision must be graded as an explicit outcome rather than inferred from a green run.

rubrics.criterion: Every caller site that currently reaches a convention through a slot lookup is rewritten to call the shared definitions directly: in script/validate-data/index.ts the properties-path resolution, the icon-reference branch, the blank-template gate, and the deployments-folder gate; in script/sync-ghes/index.ts the properties require path, the partner-creator check, the code-scanning eligibility check, the icon-kind decision, and the workflow/properties/icon path construction for the sync file list.
rubrics.rationale: Shotgun surgery is graded on the consumers as much as the implementations: leaving a consumer calling through a removed or bypassed mechanism is the failure mode that both makes the diff incomplete and leaves dangling configuration behind.

rubrics.criterion: Cross-module wiring is explicit and importable: the GHES script (and the validation script) name the shared convention module(s) in normal static imports (or require) whose resolution works under each script's own tsconfig include scope, and no script's access to a convention relies on an import performed only to register fragments as a side effect.
rubrics.rationale: The injected diff added modules flat in script/validate-data only because each script's tsconfig includes just *.ts in its own directory, so a repair that tries to place shared code in a fresh subdirectory or that relies on implicit registration ordering can typecheck one script while breaking the other — this item grades the dependency structure itself.

rubrics.criterion: The knowledge-level configuration each settings.json controls is preserved intact except for convention-selection entries that stop being consumed: for both script/validate-data/settings.json and script/sync-ghes/settings.json the folders list, allowed-categories mapping, enabledActions, partners, and readOnlyFolders still drive the same behavior as before the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The settings files are half of the injected scatter (each carries a templateRules slot map added by the diff), so they are also where a careless repair is most likely to delete or damage unrelated configuration while removing the slot maps — the graded fact is that only selection plumbing changed.

rubrics.criterion: Where an inline expression was replaced by a call into the shared conventions (for example the blank-template gate or the deployments gate in the validation sweep), the call sites keep making the same decision under the same surrounding conditions — specifically the gates are applied to the workflow being checked with its own path and folder, not to a neighboring path, a different variable, or a hoisted single result reused across loop iterations.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not broaden the shared conventions' blast radius in a way this repository cannot support: moving conventions must not add new runtime dependencies, change how either script is launched, alter script/validate-data or script/sync-ghes package.json dependency sets beyond no-op, or require the two settings files to be merged or moved.
rubrics.rationale: Each script is an independent npm project with its own package.json and tsconfig; the repository's own test entry only exercises script/validate-data, so a structural change that breaks script/sync-ghes's packaging would not be caught by the sweep and must be graded from the patch.

rubrics.criterion: The dedicated fragment modules created to hold registered rule pieces — script/validate-data/templatePaths.ts (the properties/workflow path helpers) and script/validate-data/templateIcons.ts (the icon-reference helpers) — are removed (or, if the solver deliberately folds their content into the single shared home, their former path and icon implementations no longer live as separate duplicated definitions anywhere else).

rubrics.rationale: The injected registry (in script/validate-data/templateRules.ts) carries a throw-on-missing-rule lookup and per-script slot maps; the cleanup obligation is graded as semantic dead-code removal rather than forcing deletion of a specific file, because a solver may legitimately redesign the shared home differently than the reference repair.

rubrics.criterion: The validation sweep has not become stricter or looser through the repair in ways the current catalogue cannot reveal: in particular, treating an iconName that begins with `octicon` but has no trailing name (or a value like 'not-octicon alike' that merely contains the word) as an embedded reference, or conversely subjecting genuine `octicon <name>` references to an svg-file probe (which would report every embedded reference as a missing icon), both fail this item; a plain svg name still resolves against the icons folder of the repository relative to the validation script's working directory.

rubrics.criterion: The GHES sync's file-list construction has not drifted: for every workflow classification the strings handed to git for restoring content — the workflow path `<folder>/<id>.yml`, the properties path `<folder>/properties/<id>.properties.json`, and (for svg icons) the icon path `../../icons/<name>.svg` — are byte-for-byte the same paths today's code produces, and read-only folders are still skipped from this restoration while their templates still appear in the compatibility list.

rubrics.criterion: The GHES eligibility and classification logic still matches today's outcome rule for rule: a workflow is excluded from the compatible set whenever its creator matches the partners list, independent of any enterprise flag adjustment; a creator match is still case-insensitive against the lowercase partners set; a non-partner workflow in the code-scanning folder is still excluded unless its properties set enterprise to true; and workflows meeting none of those conditions are still compatible when their used actions are allowed under the enabled-actions rule.
